reason: Tried to break it and could not. Pulled the Internet Archive full text of the Columbia 1963 edition (instructionsforp00wang) and read it in place: under the running head “30 Instructions for Practical Living” section 26 reads, in full, [The Teacher said,] “Knowledge is the beginning of action and action is the completion of knowledge. Learning to be a sage involves only one effort. Knowledge and action should not be separated.” The three sentences are the whole of the section, contiguous and verbatim, so nothing is stitched. Section 5 in the same text has the different wording (“knowledge is the beginning of action and action the completion of knowledge”, without the second is), so the verifier was right to cite 26 and not 5; Chan’s own introduction quotes the section 5 form. Part I and p. 30 are right. The bracketed [The Teacher said,] is Chan’s editorial supply and the Teacher is Wang, so the line is his own and needs no speaker. Wang Yangming is the pinyin form of the Wang Yang-ming on the title page: same person, acceptable. shipped.js: not shipped, nothing near, Wang at 0 of 3, not banned (Confucius is banned, Wang is not). In scope, publishable, on theme. Source line leads with the name, no dash, 98 characters. Tag Philosophy is the form of the work.
